correctness.rationale: The six entries of X^2 are reconstructed directly. Partition on (a,d) into four exhaustive and disjoint possibilities, rank the two equations in (e,f,g) for nonzero boundary coefficients, and count fibers of the rank-one outer-product matrix when both vanish. Every row follows with its q-factor from h,i,j or f,h,i,j, and the table accounts for all q^10 inputs. Summing target classes proves the image formula, and zero-target substitution yields 5q^6-4q^5. Characteristic two and the boundary n<=4 are explicitly proved. Exhaustive q=2 and F_4 checks verify all 64 and 4096 target fibers, respectively; these checks are finite corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The five-by-five case is the mathematically forced first failure of squaring surjectivity onto the verbal subgroup, not an arbitrarily selected small matrix size. It is natural to ask which word values occur and their exact multiplicities at the threshold. The theorem answers both uniformly over every F_{2^e}, gives a rank-one determinant obstruction on one boundary stratum, and sharpens known width-two and global lower-bound results to exact data. The fact concerns a complete natural finite invariant, useful for word-map statistics and comparing small nilpotent groups; no speculative downstream theorem is necessary.
